defects.what: Split screen: a TV with a flooded city on top and a separate empty sofa scene below, divided by a hard line.
The Bakunawa is drawn with two heads side by side in front of the red moon.
The man opening the hologram has spiky loose hair and no topknot: he does not read as Indio.
The Ucayali memory shows two unknown children (one blond) instead of Indio.
Two bare feet and a stray brown paw at the bottom; Usman is black, so the paw belongs to no one.
Japanese-style tiled roofs and paper-screen windows behind the grandmother and child.
The roofs around the bell tower are East Asian curved tile roofs.
The rainy city has narrow streets with small vertical signs that look Japanese.
The folk illustration shows two serpents/heads where the tale has one Bakunawa.
The friar's open book shows lines of pseudo-script.
